item.title: Orphaned elephant Daba adopted by herd in Kenya
item.description: On September 30, 2025, rangers from the Sheldrick Wildlife Trust and the Kenya Wildlife Service found an 8-month-old elephant alone north of the Galana River. They suspect that lions had chased away her herd, the Dabaduki group. The calf was named Daba, which means 'abandoned'. After the Voi Reintegration Unit, she was brought to the Nairobi Nursery for specialized care....

item.title: Bull elephant 'adopts' orphan calf Talek until rescue came
item.description: In June 2023, a seven-month-old orphaned elephant calf was spotted at the Maasai Mara National Reserve in Kenya. When rangers searched for her, she had disappeared. A few days later, she reappeared, this time following an older male elephant who offered her protection. Because the bull could not provide milk, the Kenya Wildlife Service authorized a rescue operation. The calf...

item.title: 12-year-old Sloan collects 30,000 diapers for Arizona food bank
item.description: For the fifth year in a row, 12-year-old Sloan from Phoenix organized her 'Diaper Drive', a diaper collection initiative. This year she aimed for 22,500 diapers, but ultimately 30,000 units arrived — so many that there was barely room to walk around in her house. The diapers, including brands such as Huggies, Pampers and Bluey, were delivered by Uhaul truck...

item.description: Pizzamas, the annual internet event by YouTubers Hank and John Green, has grown from a fan meme into a major fundraiser. It started in 2009 when John shaved on camera and fan Valerie Barr used a still to create the artwork character 'Pizza John'. item.title: Sock drive 'Socktober' celebrates 15 years of local kindness
item.description: Socktober began 15 years ago when high school students wanted to help after learning that many people in their community were homeless or shuttling between shelters. A call to the local shelter revealed that socks were desperately needed but rarely donated. Schools, churches and businesses participated, collecting more socks than could fit in a car. item.title: Tanzanian farmers return land to elephants
item.description: In the Kilombero Valley in Tanzania, 368 farmers have ceded land to provide elephants with safe passage between the Udzungwa Mountains and Nyerere National Park. After seven years of preparation by the Southern Tanzania Elephant Program (STEP) and partners, the Nyerere-Udzungwa Wildlife Corridor (NUWC) received official protection in April 2025, the first of its kind in Tanzania. item.title: Japan records 107,677 centenarians, surpassing 100,000 milestone
item.description: According to recently published figures from the Ministry of Health, Japan has 107,677 residents aged 100 or older, marking the first time the 100,000 threshold has been exceeded. This makes Japan home to the world's largest population of centenarians. When the count began in 1963, there were 153; the 1,000 mark was crossed in 1981, and 10,000 in 1998. Eighty-eight...

item.title: Students name 309-million-year-old Jeanerpeton mazonensis after their mothers
item.description: Student scientists Allison Sefcovic and Payton Kohlberg have named a newly identified early amphibian species after their mothers, both named Jean. Jeanerpeton mazonensis lived 309 million years ago, long before the dinosaurs, in the area around present-day Chicago, then a swampy river delta. The creature resembled a salamander but was stocky and pudgy like a frog. The fossil was found...

item.title: Norway protects Andfjorden: whales and coral safe
item.description: Norway established a new marine protected area on September 18: the Andfjorden Marine Protected Area, covering approximately 714 square miles (nearly 260,000 football fields). The area is located in northern Nordland and southern Troms, and encompasses waters near Andøy, Harstad and Senja. item.title: Paid photos turn Borneo hunters into orangutan protectors
item.description: On the Indonesian island of Borneo, in West Kalimantan province, residents of 9 villages can earn money by taking photos or recording sounds of wild animals. The newborn hippo lay beside the body of his mother, who had likely died while defending her calf. item.title: Ellinikon Park becomes Europe's largest coastal park
item.description: On the grounds of Athens' former airport in the southern suburbs, The Ellinikon Park is rising: two million square meters of green space that will become Europe's largest coastal urban park (200 hectares). The park is designed to actively lower ambient temperature, processes 100 percent of its own rainwater on-site, and maintains more than 520 plant species through sensor-controlled irrigation....

item.title: Clay tablet with world's oldest peace treaty discovered
item.description: Archaeologists have found a clay tablet in Turkey containing a fragment of the Treaty of Kadesh, the oldest known peace treaty in the world. The tablet, featuring articles 12 through 20, was excavated last year at the Hittite royal palace in Buyukkale, in the ancient Hittite capital Hattusa. item.title: Vietnam protects last habitat of Delacour's langur
item.description: Vietnam has established a specially protected nature reserve for the Delacour's langur, one of the world's most endangered primates. Of this species, named after the French biologist who discovered it, only around 17 populations remain, totalling approximately 250 animals. item.title: Ethical fashion brand Yes Friends secures investment from Deborah Meaden
item.description: Bristol-based clothing brand Yes Friends proves that affordable fashion can be ethical. Founded in 2021 with a sustainable T-shirt priced at £7.99, the company has expanded to include underwear and corduroy jackets, with a focus on living wages and low-impact production.
